_comment: Two providers answer the same bus methods — the Go brain by default under
DELEGATE_CATALOG_TO_BRAIN, the desktop's main process when delegation is off.
Path CONTAINMENT has contracts/path-containment-cases.json. This fixture pins the
other half of 'the same call must give the same answer': the ORDER a list comes
back in, and how each side reads a scalar that is not the type it expected.
Every block below replaced a JavaScript idiom whose Go twin behaves differently,
and each divergence was live and reachable:
order        — Go sorts strings by raw bytes (sort.Strings, `a < b`); the
desktop used localeCompare, which is case-insensitive-ish and
locale-dependent. library.list, fs.listDir and fs.listEntries
came back in stably different orders depending on which provider
answered. The order is what the picker shows and what 'first'
means in it.
scalar       — Go coerces a non-string YAML scalar with str() (-> ""); the
desktop called .localeCompare on it. `createdAt: 5`, or an
unquoted ISO date (js-yaml 4 parses that to a Date), threw inside
the comparator as soon as V8's sort put that row in the `b`
position — and the function-level catch turned the throw into an
EMPTY LIST, so every well-formed layout/session vanished with it
while the brain listed them all. <configDir>/layouts and
<configDir>/sessions are configStoreRoots, so writing that file
is an ordinary permitted fs.write.
suffix       — Go uses strings.TrimSuffix; the desktop used String#replace,
which removes the FIRST occurrence ANYWHERE. 'a.jsonl.b.jsonl'
became 'a.b.jsonl' on one side and 'a.jsonl.b' on the other — two
different resume ids for one transcript — and '.jsonlagent-x.jsonl'
became 'agent-x.jsonl', which then matched the subagent filter and
dropped a row the other provider listed. The FOLDING variant is
the library-item id: the entry filter is case-insensitive, so
'readme.Md' is listed, and trimming only '.md'/'.MD' left '.Md' on.
Owners: apps/desktop/src/main/lib/providerParity.ts (+ its call sites) and
services/hub/cmd/brain (stores.go, library.go, fsops.go, discovery.go).
THE BLOCK REGISTRY. Every array-of-objects block in this file must be declared
here and everything here must be a block — closure in both directions, so a new
block is a failure until someone says what its cases must carry, and a renamed
one cannot quietly stop being validated.
Held by cmd/brain/corpusvocab_test.go and
apps/desktop/src/main/services/contractsVocabulary.test.ts. Before those, this
kind of validation existed for exactly ONE block of ONE fixture.

order.why: The byte-order both providers must sort by.

scalar.why: The scalar-to-string rendering both providers must agree on.

suffix.why: Suffix trimming, with and without the case fold.

order.name: uppercase sorts before lowercase, byte-wise
order.why: The whole divergence in one case: localeCompare gives apple/Banana/cherry/Date, raw bytes give this. Neither is wrong on its own; having both at once is.

order.name: digits and punctuation sort by code unit, not by collation
order.why: localeCompare puts item-2 before item-10 (numeric-ish collation in several locales) and ignores the leading underscore; byte order does neither. A locale-dependent comparison also means the SAME provider can reorder itself on a different machine.

order.name: an empty string sorts first
order.why: The coerced value of a non-string scalar is "", so where empties land decides where an odd row lands — which is the difference between 'mis-sorted' and 'the list is empty'.

order.name: an astral code point sorts by UTF-8 byte, not by UTF-16 code unit
order.why: Every case above is pure ASCII, so the fixture could not see the one place `a < b` in JavaScript is NOT Go's `a < b`. A code point above U+FFFF is a UTF-16 surrogate pair whose lead unit is 0xD800-0xDBFF, so `<` sorts it BELOW everything in 0xE000-0xFFFF, while its UTF-8 encoding starts 0xF0-0xF4 and Go sorts it ABOVE the 0xE0-0xEF of the BMP. Same directory, opposite placement of the emoji entry, on fs.listDir / fs.listEntries / library.list / layouts.list / sessions.list.

scalar.name: a number is not a string
a boolean is not a string
a list is not a string
a map is not a string

suffix.name: only the SUFFIX, never the first occurrence
suffix.why: String#replace removes the first match anywhere and gives 'a.b.jsonl' — a different resume id for the same transcript.

suffix.name: a leading occurrence is not a suffix
suffix.why: replace() gives 'agent-x.jsonl', which then matches the startsWith('agent-') subagent filter and drops a row the other provider lists.

suffix.name: the whole string is the suffix
folded: mixed case
suffix.why: The entry filter that admits the file is already case-insensitive, so this file IS listed; trimming only '.md' and '.MD' left '.Md' on and minted id 'readme-md' on one side and 'readme' on the other.

suffix.name: folded: not a suffix at all
